Categories: 4 points worse, 6 points worse, 8 points worse

items.note:
First use the raw scores to explain the parameters: If you want to identify the average difference between the two groups by 4 points, and the standard deviation of the individual scores is assumed to be 10 points, the standardized difference is 0.4; the differences of 6 points and 8 points correspond to 0.6 and 0.8 respectively. These three differences and standard deviations are all teaching assumptions. There is no basis for replacing the results of this course with the results of public papers, nor are they called the default "small, medium, and large" effects in the field.
Under the premise that the two groups are independent, the number of samples is equal, the common standard deviation and the normal model, the two-sided significance level is 0.05, and the target test power is 80%, the actual number of people in each group calculated by the power.t.test of local R is 99.0803, 44.5858, 25.5246, and after rounding up, it is 100, 45, 26. The R code uses strict=TRUE to calculate the two rejection areas on both sides, and uses the numerical integration of the chi-square variance term to check the efficacy; then check that the current integer number of people reaches 80%, and it is not reached when there is one less person. Calculation source code, CSV, session version and hash are saved in design-packet.
"Efficacy 80%" means that in repeated studies where the specified difference does exist and the model and other premises are established, the probability of detection according to the specified test rules is 80%; it does not mean that the conclusion of this study has an 80% probability of being correct. 0.05 represents the control target of the probability of falsely reporting differences according to predetermined rules under the premise of zero difference; it is not the probability that the research result is false. The page does not require beginners to memorize formulas, the point is that the number depends on the basis of differences and fluctuations one wishes to identify.
On page 13, only the scene demonstration resources with a difference of 6 points are used for conversion. Formal research needs to first demonstrate why a 6-point difference is worth identifying, where the 10-point fluctuation comes from, and whether individual allocation is feasible. When changing to class allocation, the number of independent classes and intra-group correlation need to be considered; non-normality, different variances, repeated measurements, baseline adjustments or actual missingness should also be calculated separately in the final analysis. Variances and fluctuations cannot be backfilled to accommodate existing budgets, and calculations cannot be run as if the sample basis has been approved.

pairs: How does a sample plan turn into workload?
Follow the "6 points difference" teaching scenario: each group requires 45 complete main results, and then estimates the recruitment, measurement and scoring capacity.
Teaching capacity measurement: Number of students, number of students, and number of ratings have their own meanings; the 90% retention rate has not been empirically verified.
Source: R stats official description; local calculation 2026-10-19; course method description/teaching simulation
Arrangement This example calculation still needs to be confirmed
Full main results 45 people/group, total 90 people 6 points difference scenario; see page 11 for prerequisites
Recruitment reservation 45÷0.90 rounded up = 50 people/group The retention rate of 90% is a teaching assumption
Measurement schedule 100 people × 3 time points = 300 people Baseline, on site, one week later
Grading task 100 answer sheets × 2 raters = 200 times. Prepared at full capacity, but not yet actually scored.
items.note:
The resource table starts with headcount calculations, rather than listing equipment and funding out of thin air. In the 6-point difference scenario, there are 45 people in each group and a total of 90 complete main results; assuming a 90% retention rate, divide 45 by 0.90 and round up to 50 people in each group, with a total recruitment capacity of 100 people. The 10% missingness is only reserved for teaching and does not guarantee that the research will not be affected by missingness bias. If dropout is related to group or outcome, increasing the number of participants will not eliminate bias.
According to the three time points of baseline, on-site and one week later, 100 people are planned to be reserved for measurement, and the capacity is 300 people. The 300 records here are not regarded as 300 independent students, and the actual collection number will not be prefilled as 300. The main results are based on 100 answer sheets and 200 scores are reserved for two raters who do not know the grouping; the verification and handling rules for scoring differences need to be formulated separately. This is task capacity, not the amount of work that has been paid for or completed.
Official launch also requires confirmation of recruitment and data permissions, whether the test can be scheduled a week later, the availability of two raters, scoring rules and trial materials, as well as intervention content, record storage and budget. Engineering research conditions such as equipment range and material batch in the original table can still be used as resource check items in other disciplines; this page uses course research examples to demonstrate how to extrapolate from samples and measurement numbers to workload.
If the real resource only accommodates 100 people, and the difference you wish to identify is 4 points, you cannot copy the number of 45 people/group: the conditional calculation on page 11 requires 100 complete results per group. The value of the problem, estimation accuracy and detectable range should be re-discussed, and the data basis should be supplemented or postponed, instead of silently deleting controls, changing main indicators or amplifying the expected effect. All cases have not yet been recruited, collected, scored, approved, or formed into actual research results.
